frameworkName: NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
licenseNote: Public domain (U.S. Government publication). Summaries below are original, written for this application - they are not reproductions of NIST publication text.
demonstrationSubsetDisclaimer: This is an illustrative subset for portfolio demonstration purposes, not full framework coverage.

controls.title: AI governance policy and accountability structure
controls.summary: The vendor maintains a documented governance structure with clear accountability for AI system risks, including named roles responsible for oversight.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for named owners (not just a policy document) and evidence the structure is actually followed, not just written.

controls.title: Legal and regulatory compliance mapping for AI use
controls.summary: The vendor tracks applicable AI-specific legal and regulatory obligations relevant to the jurisdictions and industries it serves.
controls.validationGuidance: Evidence should reference specific regulations (e.g. EU AI Act, sector rules) rather than a generic compliance statement.

controls.title: AI system inventory and use-case documentation
controls.summary: The vendor maintains an inventory of AI/ML systems in use, including their purpose, intended use cases, and known limitations.
controls.validationGuidance: Confirm the inventory includes third-party or embedded AI models, not just internally built systems.

controls.title: Context and impact assessment for AI use cases
controls.summary: The vendor documents the operational context and potential impact (including on individuals) of each AI system before deployment.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for evidence the assessment happens before deployment, not retroactively.

controls.title: Model performance and bias testing
controls.summary: AI systems are tested for accuracy, reliability, and bias/fairness issues appropriate to their use case prior to and during deployment.
controls.validationGuidance: Bias testing evidence should be specific to the model and use case, not a generic statement of fairness commitment.

controls.title: Ongoing monitoring for model drift and degradation
controls.summary: The vendor monitors deployed AI systems over time for performance degradation, data drift, or unexpected behavior.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for a defined monitoring cadence and a process for what happens when drift is detected, not just passive logging.

controls.title: Explainability and transparency documentation
controls.summary: The vendor can provide documentation explaining how AI system outputs are generated, appropriate to the risk level of the use case.
controls.validationGuidance: Higher-risk use cases (e.g. those affecting eligibility decisions) should have more detailed explainability documentation than low-risk ones.

controls.title: Human oversight and override mechanisms
controls.summary: AI systems that inform consequential decisions include a mechanism for human review or override of automated outputs.
controls.validationGuidance: Confirm the override mechanism is actually usable in practice, not merely theoretical or buried in an approval chain.

controls.title: Incident response process for AI-specific failures
controls.summary: The vendor has a defined process for responding to AI-specific incidents, such as harmful outputs, data leakage through model behavior, or bias-driven harm.
controls.validationGuidance: Distinguish this from generic security incident response - look for AI-specific triggers and escalation paths.

controls.title: Third-party and foundation model risk management
controls.summary: Where the vendor relies on third-party or foundation AI models, it assesses and documents the risk this dependency introduces.
controls.validationGuidance: This is a common gap - many vendors build on top of third-party models without formally assessing that dependency's risk.

controls.title: AI-specific risk tolerance documented
controls.summary: The organization has documented its risk tolerance specific to AI system deployment, distinct from general IT risk tolerance.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for AI-specific thresholds (e.g. acceptable error rates for consequential decisions), not a generic risk appetite statement.

controls.title: AI system dependencies and interconnections mapped
controls.summary: The vendor documents how its AI systems interact with other systems and data flows, including upstream and downstream dependencies.
controls.validationGuidance: Ask specifically whether the map includes data flowing into the model, not only the model's outputs.
